method: Individual review against PDF pages 16–20. Anatomical and legal terms are explained as language; no medical procedures, diagnosis, liability determination or independent verification of the narrative is provided.
words: to take a substance into something
Picture a sponge taking liquid inside: absorb. Link the verb with absorption; the b changes to p in the noun's spelling.
Literal taking-in sense; teaching example avoids turning the narrated dangerous practice into instructions.
going around or avoiding a usual route or stage
by + pass suggests passing by something instead of through it. Bypass keeps both s letters before -ing.
The new system saves time by bypassing an unnecessary step.
新系统通过跳过一个不必要的步骤来节省时间。
Route-avoidance sense in the source; no medical mechanism is independently validated.
putting things into groups according to shared features
category becomes categorize, then categorizing drops final e. Imagine moving records into labeled categories.
We are categorizing the requests by topic.
我们正在按主题给这些请求分类。
Insurer groups claims by kind; not judging whether they are true.
supporting an inference indirectly through surrounding facts
间接的；依靠相关情形推断的
以间接证据构成的案情论证
circumstance means a surrounding fact or situation. Circumstantial evidence builds an inference from those surroundings rather than a direct account.
The explanation relied on circumstantial evidence.
这个解释依赖间接证据。
Does not mean false or necessarily weak; source says may have, so uncertainty must remain.
facts that support a conclusion indirectly rather than directly showing it
Evidence is uncountable: say some circumstantial evidence, not an evidence. Link circumstance with the surrounding facts used to infer a conclusion.
The investigators considered the circumstantial evidence.
调查人员考虑了这些间接证据。
An evidentiary description in the narration, not a judgment that an allegation is proved.
a request for payment under an insurance policy
Claim can be an assertion, but an insurance claim asks for payment. Picture a claim form sent to an insurer.
She filed a claim after the damage was discovered.
发现损坏后，她提出了索赔。
Insurer's sample of liability claims, not merely assertions or ownership claims.
procedures in which liquid is introduced into the rectum
Enema has three syllables, EN-uh-muh; add -s pronounced /z/ for enemas. Recognize it as an anatomical/procedural term, not a drink.
The report discussed the use of enemas.
报告讨论了灌肠的使用。
Source alleges dangerous nonmedical use; definition only, with no procedural guidance or endorsement.
instances of physical harm to the body
injury changes consonant + y to -ies: injuries. Connect injured with the person and injuries with the harm.
The report recorded several serious injuries.
报告记录了几起严重受伤情况。
Physical harm in the hazing discussion, not insults or reputational damage.
taken or moved somewhere very quickly because it was urgent
rush ends in /ʃ/, so rushed adds /t/, not a separate syllable. Picture an urgent movement, not a relaxed journey.
The injured man was rushed to the hospital.
受伤的男子被紧急送往医院。
Passive emergency-transport meaning; unrelated to fraternity recruitment rush in this sentence.
subjected to anal intercourse, here in a suspected sexual-assault context
（此语境）被怀疑遭到肛交性侵的
sodomize drops final e before -ed: sodomized. Remember the /zd/ ending and the passive was sodomized in the attributed report.
The report said doctors initially suspected that the patient had been sodomized.
报告称，医生起初怀疑患者遭到了肛交性侵。
Initially thought marks a preliminary suspicion, not a confirmed finding. Technical/explicit receptive vocabulary; no graphic elaboration.
terrify keeps y before -ing: terrifying. Terrifying describes what causes fear; terrified describes the person who feels it.
Getting lost in the storm was a terrifying experience.
在暴风雨中迷路是一次可怕的经历。
News is fear-inducing; the news itself is not frightened.
a physical attack or threat of violence against someone
Anchor assault in an attack, then contrast with insult, hurtful words. In assault and battery, battery does not mean an electrical battery.
The report described an alleged assault.
报告描述了一起被指称的袭击。
General-language gloss for an insurance category; precise legal distinctions vary and are not adjudicated here.
marking skin with a heated object
烙印；用热物在皮肤上留下标记
Brand can be a mark, not just a product name. Branding here creates a physical mark; contrast it with company branding in marketing.
The report described injuries caused by branding.
报告描述了烙印造成的伤害。
Physical injury sense, not corporate image-building; no how-to instruction.
lasting harm to someone's feelings or emotional well-being
emotion + -al describes feelings; damage is uncountable harm. Connect emotional damage with feelings rather than broken objects.
The experience caused lasting emotional damage.
这段经历造成了持久的心理伤害。
Source contrasts physical/aesthetic consequences with emotional effects; no diagnosis of a specific person.
pieces of tissue transferred to repair or replace damaged tissue
Picture graft as a patch transferred to a damaged area. In skin grafts, graft is a medical tissue term, not corruption.
The article mentioned patients who needed skin grafts.
文章提到了需要植皮的患者。
Skin-repair sense; not instructions for treatment.
court cases concerning alleged harmful initiation practices
Hazing modifies lawsuits to identify the issue; lawsuits is the plural of law + suit. Filing a lawsuit is not the same as winning it.
The university faced several hazing lawsuits.
这所大学面临数起涉及入会欺凌的诉讼。
Narrator stresses that a small share of claims does not mean few incidents.
a strong metallic element used to make tools and structures
Iron is usually pronounced like EYE-ern in American English, not eye-ron. Attach the word to the metal in an iron tool.
The old gate was made of iron.
Material in hot iron tool, not the action of smoothing clothes.
lasting rather than temporary or expected to end soon
Pair permanent with temporary as opposites. A permanent mark stays; keep -nent at the end, not -nate.
The leak caused permanent damage to the floor.
漏水给地板造成了永久性损坏。
Duration of harm described in source; not an independently confirmed prognosis.
a person or organization bringing a civil court case against another
Link plaintiff with complaint: the plaintiff brings the complaint to court. Keep double f at the end and contrast with defendant.
The plaintiff filed a complaint against the company.
原告对这家公司提起了诉讼。
Claimant role, not necessarily a proven victim or a prosecutor.
a prospective member undergoing a fraternity's joining process
兄弟会准成员；入会新人
Pledge can mean a promise; here it names the person beginning membership. Remember new pledge to keep the person sense distinct.
The club welcomed its new pledges.
该社团欢迎新入会的准成员。
Person, not a promise or donation; very bright-minded is sarcasm in the source.
the final part of the large intestine before the anus
Learn rectum as a precise anatomy label and stress REC-. Distinguish the rectum inside the body from the anus, the opening.
Anatomical vocabulary needed to understand the reported injury; no procedural instruction.
to suffer or experience an injury or loss
Sustain can mean keep going, but sustain an injury means suffer it. Memorize the whole verb-object pair instead of using one translation everywhere.
The building sustained damage during the storm.
这栋建筑在暴风雨中遭到损坏。
Sustain injuries is the suffer sense, not support or maintain.
platforms projecting from a building above ground level, usually with railings
balcony changes y to -ies in the plural balconies. Picture several small platforms along a building.
Plural building structures in the list of fall locations.
affected by alcohol or another substance, especially drunk
醉酒的；受酒精等影响的
Connect intoxicate with toxic to recall a substance affecting the body. Intoxicated is formal; drunk is the everyday equivalent in this passage.
The report said the driver appeared intoxicated.
报告称，司机看起来处于醉酒状态。
Alcohol context; teaching example retains reported appearance rather than a diagnosis.
people or organizations bringing civil court cases against others
plaintiff ends in /f/, so plural -s is /s/. Compare plaintiffs, who bring a case, with defendants, who answer it.
Plural legal role; filing a claim does not establish its truth.
usual or generally accepted as normal
Stand a regular example beside unusual ones: it is the standard. Learn standard practice to recall the adjective sense.
Checking the list is standard practice.
The speaker explicitly does not know whether the practice is standard, so avoid converting it into a universal claim.
a sequence of actions or events through which something happens
Remember process as steps happening one after another. In the process can mean while that was happening, without implying a formal procedure.
The box was damaged in the process of moving it.
箱子在搬运过程中损坏了。
Temporal phrase within the alleged events, not a legal summons or software process.
a route or means of getting out of danger, here part of fire escape
逃生通道；（fire escape）消防逃生梯
Escape means get out of danger; a fire escape is the structure used to do that. Learn the whole compound so fire does not become the thing escaping.
The building has an external fire escape.
这栋楼有外置消防逃生梯。
Noun within fire escapes, not the standalone verb escape in this sentence.
producing a useful or favorable effect
benefit becomes beneficial. The -cial ending sounds /ʃəl/; connect the adjective with a benefit received.
The change could be beneficial to students.
这项改变可能对学生有益。
Financial advantage alleged for institutions, not necessarily moral or educational benefit.
made information known that was previously private or unknown
disclose + d gives disclosed. Link disclose with reveal; contrast disclosed with undisclosed to remember the negative prefix un-.
The full amount was not disclosed.
Source refers to donations; not disclosed does not itself imply illegality.
money or goods given to support a person or organization
donate drops final e before -ion: donation. The donor gives; the donation is what is given.
They made a donation to the scholarship fund.
他们向奖学金基金捐了款。
Financial contributions to institutions; no actual amount or donor identity verified.
attractive enough to make someone want something
entice drops final e before -ing: enticing. Enticing describes the attraction; enticed describes the person drawn in.
The flexible schedule made the offer more enticing.
灵活的时间安排让这份提议更有吸引力。
Speaker sarcastically contrasts party attractions with academic costs; not an endorsement of dangerous activities.
in relation to money or financial resources
financial + -ly gives financially. It answers in what respect: financially beneficial means beneficial in money terms.
这个项目在财务上可以持续运转。
Narrows beneficial to monetary benefit, not overall social value.
the fraternity and sorority system and associated social activities at US colleges
美国大学兄弟会、姐妹会体系及其社交生活
参与兄弟会或姐妹会活动
Greek points to Greek-letter organization names, not Greece as a location. Picture letter-named campus organizations to recall Greek life.
She wrote an article about Greek life on campus.
她写了一篇有关校园兄弟会和姐妹会生活的文章。
Corrects literal 希腊生活 interpretation; covers both fraternity and sorority organizations.
homes or accommodation provided for people
house becomes housing, with /z/ in the middle and no final e. Housing is usually uncountable, unlike individual houses.
The university plans to expand student housing.
大学计划增加学生住宿设施。
something that encourages a person or organization to act
Pair incentive with incentive to + verb: a benefit creates a reason to act. Picture a reward attached to an action.
Lower costs provide an incentive to share resources.
降低成本为共享资源提供了动力。
Bottom-line incentive is a financial motivation, not an instruction or guaranteed result.
an established organization such as a university
Institute and institution belong to the same word family. In this passage, picture a university rather than an abstract social custom.
The institution offers several scholarship programs.
这所机构提供多项奖学金计划。
Refers to colleges/universities, not hospitalization or a custom.
to keep something in good condition through regular care
maintenance is the noun related to maintain. Keep the second syllable stressed in maintain and picture regular repairs that keep a building usable.
The school pays to maintain the buildings.
学校支付建筑维护费用。
Building upkeep, not asserting an opinion or maintaining innocence.
activities used to promote something and attract customers or users
market + -ing names the activity of reaching a market. Here prospective students are the audience, not shoppers at a street market.
The team discussed its marketing strategy.
Attracting students through social-life appeal, as proposed by the speaker.
people who formerly attended or graduated from a school or university
Alumni is a traditional plural: alumnus is singular masculine, alumna feminine. Remember the plural ending sounds /naɪ/ and use alumni are.
Many alumni returned for the reunion.
许多校友回来参加了聚会。
Former students, not current students or aluminum; the alleged donation finding remains attributed.
a local branch of a larger organization
A chapter is one part of a whole: in a book a section, in an organization a local branch. Here houses anchors the branch sense.
The chapter rents a house near campus.
这个分会在校园附近租了一栋房子。
Same branch sense as Unit 4, separately retained for this Unit's housing context.
buildings or rooms where students live, short for dormitories
Dorm is the shortened form of dormitory. Add plural -s /z/ after /m/: dorms.
Most first-year students live in the dorms.
大多数一年级学生住在宿舍。
Student accommodation, not classrooms; source's less buildings is not copied into the teaching model.
combined to become one organization or whole
merge already ends in e, so add d: merged. Keep /dʒd/ at the end; picture two groups becoming one.
The two departments merged into one.
两个部门合并成了一个。
Historical claim reported with apparently; no independent verification of the organizations' dates.
money paid for instruction at a school or university
Connect tuition with tutor: both relate to teaching. In American college context tuition usually means the price of instruction, not housing costs.
The scholarship covers tuition but not housing.
奖学金支付学费，但不支付住宿费。
More tuition means increased tuition revenue from more admitted students, not more teaching sessions.
willing to give more money, help, or resources than expected
Connect generous with generosity: the adjective describes the giver, the noun the quality. Anchor both to giving rather than the unrelated general.
The alumni were generous with their support.
校友们慷慨地提供了支持。
Financial giving to former universities; source's research claim remains qualified, not independently established.
